admission.justification: The flat per-action split and the subject-folder layout were both built and compared; the choice binds where every future l-01 detail file goes.

alternatives.option: Group detail files in subject folders (reference/<subject>/, with <subject>/<role>/ beside <subject>/shared/), name each file by what it holds, write a rule of one or two sentences inline at its action, and give a file only to content that costs more than its pointer.
alternatives.reason: Fewer and larger files are read at the step that needs them, and short rules reach the agent without a tool call.

alternatives.option: One topic file per action or heading group, split from the working-rules files into one flat reference folder.
alternatives.reason: It produced many very small files whose pointers cost as much as their rules, with no folder rule and no lower size bound.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Reader runs show agents open small single-action files but skip grouped files at the step that needs them.

consequences: Every pointer, manifest entry, packaged copy, budget record and test follows a moved file in the same change.
The memory's skill-writing guideline carries the folder and naming rules.
context: Splitting the catch-all reference files into one topic file per action left 74 files in one flat folder, 34 of them coord-topic-<role>-<topic>.md and 39 under 150 words. A pointer was often nearly as long as the rule it led to, and an agent spends a tool call on every file it opens.
